title: Empirical Margin Sensitivity: An Interventional Neuron-Level Probe of Post-Trained Medical LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.30675v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Medical post-training raises benchmark accuracy, but accuracy does not show which internal components a model's decisions depend on, or whether components that support one benchmark also support another. We apply the weight-space intervention paradigm of ROME and MEMIT at the granularity of one MLP down-projection column. Our measurement, Empirical Margin Sensitivity (EMS), replaces each coordinate magnitude of a column by its mean while preserving the column's sign pattern and L1 scale, and records the resulting change in the logit margin between the correct option and its hardest-wrong competitor. This isolates the margin's dependence on a column's fine-grained coordinate structure while the column stays in place. We discover high-EMS columns (anchors) on MedQA in ten public checkpoints (four general-purpose bases and six medical post-trained variants) across the Gemma, Llama, Qwen, and AFM families, and measure the same columns on Med

translated_title: 经验边际敏感性：对后训练医疗大语言模型的干预式神经元级探针

tldr: 该论文提出经验边际敏感性（EMS）这一神经元级干预探针，在MLP下投影列粒度上探测后训练医疗大模型的决策内部依赖，并在多个模型家族中发现了跨基准的高敏感“锚点”列。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Empirical Margin Sensitivity (EMS), an interventional neuron-level probe that measures how post-trained medical LLMs' decisions depend on individual MLP down-projection columns and discovers high-sensitivity "anchor" columns across medical benchmarks and model families.
